text:
Alex: Hey finance team — I just noticed a charge on my corp card:
Alex: SkyHigh Airlines - FARE UPGRADE $320.00. Merchant shows as SKYHIGH*UPGRADE. I used points to upgrade but the charge still posted. Need to file this in Expensify.
Maria: @Alex can you attach the itemized e-ticket and the boarding pass? We need to see base fare vs upgrade. If it was points, might be personal.
Alex: Attaching screenshot of the charge and the confirmation email (will upload to Expensify after clarifying). The email shows:
```
Order: 998271
Base Fare: $420.00
Seat Upgrade (paid): $320.00
Miles used: 25k
```
Samir: If miles were used + a paid upgrade charge posted, that suggests partial redemption + cash top-up. Policy: upgrades paid by employee are personal unless manager pre-approval recorded.
JESS: Hi @Alex — Finance needs three things to process: itemized receipt showing line items, manager approval for the paid upgrade (if personal portion), and confirmation whether you used a personal card + were reimbursed. If it's fully corporate (pre-approved travel class) we can code to travel:airfare.
Alex: I didn't get explicit pre-approval for the upgrade. Used corp card to pay the upgrade because it was a last-minute gate purchase. Manager pinged me later saying it's fine but I don't have an approval email.
Maria: @Olivia (your manager) — can you confirm here whether you approve the $320 upgrade as business expense? :pleading_face:
Olivia: Confirming I verbally approved due to client meeting schedule, but I don't have an email thread. Happy to approve now for reimbursement of the full amount. If finance needs written confirmation, I can reply-all with approval.
JESS: Thanks @Olivia. For audit we need a short email or Slack thread from manager that explicitly approves the upgrade on the corp card. Once that's in Expensify we can code full $320 to travel:airfare. If manager wants the company to absorb only base fare, we can split the transaction — finance can process a personal-payback for the upgrade portion.
Alex: I'll ask Olivia to drop a quick approval email and I'll upload the e-ticket + boarding pass.
Financebot: Reminder: Corpcard disputes must be initiated within 60 days of transaction. Run `finance export-transactions --tx 998271` to pull full merchant descriptor.
Samir: Also note merchant naming mismatch can delay reconciliation (SKYHIGH vs SKYHIGH*UPGRADE). Finance will map merchant to airline once we have the e-ticket.
Maria: Quick checklist for @Alex: 1) upload itemized e-ticket 2) manager approval email (or Slack OK + manager sends email) 3) indicate whether you want full reimbursement or split personal portion.
Alex: Got it — I'll upload everything by EOD. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Olivia: Sent approval via email to finance@redwood.com with subject "Approval: Alex upgrade reimbursement" and cc'd Alex.
JESS: Received the email. Once the e-ticket is in Expensify I'll process. Expect reconciliation in next payroll cycle if all docs present.
Alex: Uploaded docs to Expensify and marked expense as "pending manager approval" (now approved). Thanks all.
